subject: Observability handoff: evidence routing and SIEM probe auth
messages:
From: Lara Nguyen <security@acmecloud.com>
To: hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai
Cc: splunk-onboarding@acmecloud.com
Date: Mon, 19 Feb 2029 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Observability handoff: evidence routing and SIEM probe auth

Hi Hiro,

Quick note from the AcmeCloud security team as we prepare the private deployment handoff:
- We need a clear path for evidence (logs, traces, metrics) to reach our SIEM and archive. For our on-prem environment we prefer either a push to an internal Splunk HEC endpoint (mTLS preferred) or an SFTP drop to a locked host that our security team pulls from.
- We also need guidance on authentication rotation policy (how Redwood expects to rotate HEC tokens / mTLS certs) and an acceptance test payload schema so we can validate integrity and field mappings.
- Finally, can you share the recommended tracing hook snippet and the default sampling guidance for our app servers? We want to make sure trace identifiers align with our correlation keys.

Timeline: we are targeting a POC acceptance window next week (Feb 26) and would like a short checklist we can sign off against.

Thanks,
Lara Nguyen
Senior Information Security Engineer
AcmeCloud

--
Note: attachments for this thread will be uploaded to our secure onboarding bucket; please list expected filenames so we can match them up.
From: hiro_tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Nguyen <security@acmecloud.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Feb 2029 13:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Observability handoff: evidence routing and SIEM probe auth

Lara — thanks for the clear ask. TL;DR: we support two robust patterns (push to a customer-managed HEC endpoint with mTLS or token + SFTP push fallback). I attached: evidence_schema_v2.csv and tracehook-snippet.py to accelerate your POC checks.

Details / options:
1) Splunk HEC (recommended for low-latency events)
   - Auth: mTLS (preferred) OR HEC token with short TTL. For hosted HEC tokens we recommend rotating every 7 days for POC and every 24 hours for production automation. If you use mTLS, present a CA-signed cert; we accept PEM chains.
   - Network: HEC behind an internal LB; allow Redwood egress IPs (we will share a CIDR set via the onboarding Drive link) OR establish a private peering tunnel.
   - Acceptance: push 3 sample events (see evidence_schema_v2.csv) and verify indexing+timestamp alignment.

2) SFTP drop (recommended for air-gapped / restrictive networks)
   - Flow: Redwood packages hourly compressed bundles and writes to an SFTP account you provision. Your security team can pull at any cadence.
   - Integrity: we sign bundles with an HMAC using a rotating key (rotation cadence configurable; default 7 days).

3) Enclave-presigned upload (hybrid)
   - If you prefer push but can't expose HEC, we can accept uploads to a presigned S3 endpoint in an enclave the customer controls. This still uses short-lived credentials and preserves auditability.

Tracing hooks and sampling:
   - Attached tracehook-snippet.py: a lightweight opentelemetry-style wrapper we recommend. Default sampling for POC: 10% for application-level spans; for high-volume collectors (ingest tier) we recommend 1% as baseline and then bump by route for problem areas.
   - Correlation: we can accept a custom header X-Acme-Corr-Id; the tracehook includes a small transformer to copy that into the root span.

Acceptance checklist (high level):
   - Network connectivity verified (HEC mTLS handshake OR SFTP transfer)
   - Sample payloads (3 examples) successfully indexed in your SIEM
   - Signed bundle verification (if SFTP)
   - Trace spans sampled and correlated to request IDs for 3 traced requests

Next steps:
   - If OK, please share a minimal network diagram and where you'd like the push target to be documented. I created JIRA-OBS-1243 to track acceptance; I'll drop the acceptance test plan into the Drive link (OBS-1243-acceptance-plan).
   - Proposed sync: Wed 21 Feb 10:00 PT to review results.

Attaching: evidence_schema_v2.csv; tracehook-snippet.py

Best,
Hiro Tanaka
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 20 Feb 2029 08:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Observability handoff: evidence routing and SIEM probe auth

Couple of quick clarifications for the POC checklist we should confirm before the Wed sync:
- Retention: Acme has requested a 90-day raw-events retention for the POC window. Can Redwood mark incoming HEC events with a metadata tag (redwood_receipt_ts) so your SIEM can run retention rules?
- PII masking: We should recommend a default field mask set; I'll attach a sample redaction list to the Drive link.

Also, Diego — can you validate the HEC mTLS code path in the tracehook/snippet for cert reloads? We should confirm the client cert rotation logic will survive a cert change without dropping telemetry for > 60s.

Kimberly
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 21 Feb 2029 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Observability handoff: evidence routing and SIEM probe auth

Thanks, Hiro and team — that plan looks good. A few notes from our side: 
- We will enable an internal Splunk HEC endpoint with mTLS (certificate will be managed by our infra team). We will also create an SFTP fallback account and drop a small sample bundle there for you.
- I uploaded the site network diagram (site-network-diagram.pdf) to the shared onboarding bucket and shared the link in the JIRA-OBS-1243 comments.
- Regarding sampling: we want to start POC at 5% application sampling and 1% ingest sampling, then target 1% app sampling for steady state if volume permits.
- Retention: we'll apply your recommended redwood_receipt_ts tag; Acme will retain raw events for 90 days as requested.

Action items for Redwood: please confirm the IPs we will see from your egress pool so our firewall rule can be staged. Also, Diego — if you can sanity-check the cert reload behavior that Kimberly flagged before Wed's sync that would be great.

We will provision the SFTP account and notify splunk-onboarding with credentials via the secure channel (not by email).

Lara
Senior Information Security Engineer | AcmeCloud
